detail.title: Institutional Journal: Error-Correction Mechanisms in Information Survival
detail.summary: We have assessed the role of formal error detection as a requisite for institutional information survival. Information decay is not merely an entropic drift but an operational failure to correct deviation. Current evidence confirms that persistence in technical, genetic, and institutional systems requires redundant, falsifiable error-correction processes. Our research indicates that observer calibration—a cognitive equivalent to error correction—is central to maintaining the stability of self-models and information structures over time.
